verses.text: Paul, called by God to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and our bro Sosthenes—
To the church of God in Corinth, to those set apart in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with everyone everywhere who calls on Jesus—He’s their Lord and ours:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I’m always thanking God for you, ‘cause of the grace He gave you through Jesus.
You’ve been loaded up in Him—with all speech and all knowledge.
The testimony of Christ is locked in among you.
So you’re not lacking any spiritual gift while you wait for Jesus to show up.
He’ll keep you steady till the end—blameless when Jesus returns.
God is faithful. He called you into this deep connection with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
Fam, I’m begging you in Jesus’ name—be on the same page. No beef, no cliques. Be united in mind and purpose.
I heard from Chloe’s people that y’all got drama—some serious division.
Some of you are like, “I’m with Paul,” or “I’m with Apollos,” or “I’m with Peter,” or “I’m Team Christ.”
Is Christ split up? Did Paul get crucified for you? Did you get baptized in my name?
I’m glad I didn’t baptize any of y’all except Crispus and Gaius—
So no one can say I baptized you in my own name.
Oh yeah—I also baptized Stephanas’ household. Can’t remember if I baptized anyone else.
Christ didn’t send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel—not with fancy words, or the cross would lose its power.
The message of the cross sounds dumb to those dying—but to us being saved, it’s the power of God.
Scripture says: “I’ll destroy the wisdom of the wise and cancel the cleverness of the clever.”
Where’s the wise one? The scholar? The debater? God made the world’s wisdom look foolish.
Since the world didn’t find God through its own wisdom, God used what looked like foolish preaching to save those who believe.
Jews want signs. Greeks want wisdom.
But we preach Christ crucified—a scandal to Jews, nonsense to Gentiles.
But to those called—Jews and Greeks—Christ is God’s power and God’s wisdom.
God’s “foolishness” is wiser than human genius. God’s “weakness” is stronger than human strength.
Look at your own calling, fam—not many of you were wise by the world’s standards, or powerful, or high-status.
But God chose the foolish to shame the wise. He picked the weak to shame the strong.
He chose the nobodies, the nothings, the overlooked—to cancel out what the world calls something.
So nobody can flex in front of God.
You’re in Christ because of God. Jesus became our wisdom, righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
So if you’re gonna brag, brag on the Lord—just like Scripture says.
When I pulled up to y’all, fam, I didn’t come with big words or flexed-out wisdom—I came raw with God’s truth.
I made up my mind to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ—and Him crucified.
I came weak, shook, and trembling.
My words weren’t polished TED Talk vibes—they came with Spirit power, not human hype.
So your faith wouldn’t rest on human genius, but on God’s power.
We do speak wisdom among the mature—but not the world’s kind, or the rulers who are fading out.
We speak God’s secret wisdom—a hidden cheat code from before time, meant to flex His glory in us.
None of the world’s rulers got it—if they had, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.
But it’s like Scripture says: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no mind imagined what God’s got ready for those who love Him.”
But God revealed it to us by His Spirit. The Spirit searches everything—even God’s deepest thoughts.
Who knows what’s in a person’s mind except their own spirit? Same with God—only His Spirit knows Him fully.
We didn’t get the world’s spirit—we got the Spirit from God, so we can know what He’s freely given us.
We speak this not with human-taught words, but Spirit-taught ones—explaining spiritual truth with Spirit language.
People without the Spirit don’t get the things of God—they sound like nonsense. They can’t understand it ‘cause it’s spiritually decoded.
But the spiritual person sees through everything, while no one can fully judge them.
“Who’s known the mind of the Lord to teach Him?” But we—we’ve got the mind of Christ.
Fam, I couldn’t talk to you like spiritual grownups—but like babies in Christ, still on formula.
I gave you milk, not meat—you weren’t ready for solid food. Still aren’t.
You’re still acting worldly. Jealousy, beef, division? That’s baby mode.
One says, “I’m with Paul,” another, “I’m with Apollos”—aren’t y’all acting like regular folks?
Who’s Apollos? Who’s Paul? Just servants who helped you believe—each doing what God assigned.
I planted, Apollos watered—but God made it grow.
So neither the planter nor the waterer is anything—it’s all God who brings the growth.
The one planting and the one watering are on the same team—and each gets paid for their part.
We’re co-workers with God. You’re God’s field. God’s building.
By God’s grace, I laid the foundation like a master builder. Others build on it—but watch how you build.
No one can lay a different foundation than what’s already laid—Jesus Christ.
If you build on that with gold, silver, jewels—or wood, hay, straw—
Your work will show up. The Day will expose it. Fire will test what kind of work it is.
If your build survives, you’ll get rewarded.
If it burns up, you’ll take a loss—but you’ll still be saved, just barely—like someone escaping a fire.
Don’t you know you’re God’s temple, and His Spirit lives in you?
If anyone wrecks God’s temple, God will wreck them—‘cause His temple is holy, and that’s you.
Don’t fool yourself. If you think you’re wise by the world’s standards, become a fool so you can get real wisdom.
The world’s wisdom is trash to God. Scripture says, “He catches the wise in their own game.”
And again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise—that they’re empty.”
So no more flexing about human leaders. Everything’s already yours—
Whether Paul, Apollos, Peter, the world, life, death, present, future—it’s all yours.
And you belong to Christ. And Christ belongs to God.
Think of us as Christ’s crew—managers of God’s secret sauce.
And what’s required of managers? Be trustworthy.
I don’t care if y’all judge me—or any human court. I don’t even judge myself.
My conscience is clear, but that doesn’t make me innocent. God’s the one who judges me.
So don’t judge anything before the time—wait till the Lord shows up. He’ll expose what’s hidden and reveal motives. Then everyone will get their praise from God.
Fam, I’ve used myself and Apollos as examples so you learn not to go beyond what’s written. No flexing one leader over another.
Who made you special? What do you have that you didn’t receive? And if you received it, why act like you earned it?
Y’all already feel full. Already rich. Already reigning—without us. I wish you really were reigning, so we could reign with you.
I think God put us apostles last—like prisoners on display, sentenced to death. We’ve become a whole spectacle to the world, angels, and humans.
We’re fools for Christ, but you’re so wise in Him. We’re weak, you’re strong. You’re honored, we’re clowned.
To this very moment, we’re hungry, thirsty, ragged, beat up, homeless.
We work with our hands. When people curse us, we bless. When persecuted, we endure.
When slandered, we answer kindly. We’ve become the world’s trash—scum of the earth, even now.
I’m not writing this to shame you, but to warn you like a dad would his kids.
You might have ten thousand tutors in Christ, but not many fathers. I became your spiritual dad through the gospel.
So I’m begging you—copy me.
That’s why I’m sending Timothy—my faithful son in the Lord. He’ll remind you how I live in Christ, just like I teach everywhere.
Some of y’all got cocky, thinking I won’t come back.
But I will come soon, if the Lord lets me—and I’ll check not just their talk, but their power.
‘Cause the kingdom of God isn’t about talk—it’s about power.
So what’s the vibe? Should I pull up with a rod, or with love and a gentle spirit?
Word on the street is there’s wild sexual sin among y’all—stuff even the pagans wouldn’t touch. A dude’s sleeping with his stepmom.
And y’all are puffed up instead of mourning? That man should’ve been cut off from the squad.
I’m not there physically, but I’m with you in spirit—and I’ve already passed judgment like I was there.
When you gather in Jesus’ name, and I’m there in spirit, with His power—
Hand that man over to Satan for the destruction of his flesh, so his spirit might be saved on the Lord’s Day.
Y’all bragging? Not it. Don’t you know a little yeast works through the whole batch of dough?
Clean out the old yeast so you can be fresh dough—because you are unleavened. Christ, our Passover Lamb, was sacrificed for us.
So let’s celebrate—not with old yeast, or the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote you before not to hang with sexually immoral people—
Not meaning folks outside the church who are immoral, greedy, scammers, or idol worshipers—otherwise you’d have to leave the world.
I meant don’t associate with anyone who claims to be a believer but lives wild—sexually immoral, greedy, idol-chasing, trash-talking, drunk, or abusive. Don’t even eat with them.
It’s not my job to judge outsiders. But aren’t we supposed to judge those inside the squad?
God handles the outsiders. But you—kick that wicked person out from among you.
How you gonna take your squadmate to court in front of unbelievers instead of letting the saints settle it?
Don’t you know the saints will judge the world? And if you’re judging the world, can’t you handle small beefs?
Don’t you know we’ll judge angels? So why not everyday stuff?
If you’ve got disputes, why bring in outsiders with no standing in the church?
I’m saying this to shame y’all. Is there really no one wise enough among you to settle this in-house?
But no—bro’s suing bro, and in front of unbelievers at that.
Just the fact that you’re suing each other means you’ve already lost. Why not just take the L? Why not be wronged?
But instead, you’re doing the wronging—and to your own people.
Don’t you know the unrighteous won’t inherit God’s kingdom? Don’t get it twisted:
No sexually wild folks, idol chasers, cheaters, flamboyant players, thieves, greedy types, drunkards, trash-talkers, or scammers will inherit the kingdom.
And that’s what some of y’all *were*. But you got washed, made holy, and cleared—by Jesus and the Spirit of our God.
“I can do anything”—yeah, but not everything’s good for you. “I can do anything”—but I won’t be mastered by anything.
“Food for the stomach and stomach for food”—sure, but God’s gonna shut both down. The body’s not for sexual sin—it’s for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
God raised the Lord and He’ll raise us too by His power.
Don’t you know your bodies are parts of Christ? Should I take Christ’s body and link it to a prostitute? No way.
Don’t know you know if you hook up with a prostitute, you become one body? Scripture says, “The two will become one flesh.”
But whoever’s joined to the Lord is one spirit with Him.
Run from sexual sin. Every other sin is outside the body, but this one hits your own body.
Don’t you know your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who lives in you and came from God? You’re not your own.
You were bought with a price. So glorify God with your body.
About what y’all asked: yeah, it’s chill to stay single.
But ‘cause of all the wild temptation out here, each guy should have his own wife, and each girl her own man.
Husbands, give your wife what’s due. Wives, same to your man.
The wife doesn’t own her body—her husband does. And the husband doesn’t own his body—his wife does.
Don’t hold out on each other unless you both agree to fast and pray. Then come back together so Satan doesn’t use your lack of self-control.
I’m saying this as a suggestion, not a command.
I wish everyone could stay single like me—but each person’s got their own gift from God.
To the singles and widows: it’s good to stay single like me.
But if you can’t control yourself, get married. Better to marry than burn with desire.
To the married, I give this command—not from me, but from the Lord: a wife shouldn’t leave her husband.
But if she does, she should stay single or reconcile. And the husband shouldn’t ditch his wife.
To the rest, I (not the Lord) say: if a believer’s married to an unbeliever who wants to stay, don’t bounce.
Same for a woman with an unbelieving husband—if he’s down to stay, don’t leave him.
‘Cause the unbelieving spouse is made holy by the believer. Otherwise, your kids would be unclean—but now they’re holy.
But if the unbeliever bounces, let them go. You’re not chained. God called us to live in peace.
How do you know, wife, if you’ll save your husband? Or you, husband, if you’ll save your wife?
Each person should live the life the Lord gave them—the one they were in when God called them. That’s what I teach everywhere.
Were you circumcised when called? Don’t try to undo it. Uncircumcised? Don’t try to get circumcised.
Circumcision or not doesn’t matter—what matters is keeping God’s commands.
Stay in the lane you were in when God called you.
Were you a slave when called? Don’t stress it. But if you can get free, go for it.
If you were a slave when called, you’re the Lord’s freed one. If you were free, you’re now Christ’s servant.
You were bought with a price—don’t become slaves to people.
Stay in your lane with God, fam.
About virgins—I’ve got no direct command from the Lord, but I’ll drop some wisdom as someone trustworthy.
I think, ‘cause of the current chaos, it’s good to stay as you are.
Got a wife? Don’t try to ditch her. Single? Don’t rush to get cuffed.
But if you do marry, you’re not sinning. Just know marriage brings challenges—and I’m trying to spare you.
Fam, time’s short. From now on, even those with spouses should live like they don’t.
Those who cry, rejoice, or buy—don’t get too attached.
Use the world, but don’t get owned by it. This world’s system is fading.
I want you free from distractions. The single guy’s focused on pleasing the Lord.
The married guy’s split—trying to please his wife too.
Same with women. The single girl’s focused on being holy in body and spirit. The married girl’s got her husband on her mind.
I’m saying this to help you—not trap you. I want you fully devoted to the Lord without distractions.
If a guy feels like he’s not doing right by his fiancée, and it’s getting intense—let them marry. It’s not sin.
But if he’s solid, not pressured, and chooses to stay single—he’s doing great too.
So the one who marries does well. The one who doesn’t? Even better.
A wife’s bound to her husband as long as he lives. If he dies, she’s free to remarry—but only in the Lord.
In my opinion, she’s better off staying single. And I think I’ve got the Spirit of God on this.
About food offered to idols—we all got knowledge. But knowledge puffs up. Love builds up.
If you think you know it all, you probably don’t.
But if you love God, He knows you.
So yeah, eating food offered to idols—we know idols are fake. There’s only one real God.
Even if people call things “gods”—in heaven or on earth, like there’s a bunch of so-called gods and lords—
For us, there’s one God—the Father, source of everything, and we live for Him. And one Lord—Jesus Christ, through whom all things exist, including us.
But not everyone knows this. Some still think the idol’s real, so when they eat that food, their conscience gets wrecked.
Food doesn’t bring us closer to God. We’re not better off if we eat—or worse if we don’t.
But be careful—your freedom might trip up someone with a weaker conscience.
If someone sees you, with your knowledge, eating in an idol’s temple, won’t they think it’s okay to do the same—even if it messes them up?
That weak believer, the one Christ died for, could fall ‘cause of your flex.
When you sin against your fam and mess with their conscience, you’re sinning against Christ.
So if food makes my sibling stumble, I’ll never eat meat again. I’m not trying to trip them up.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus our Lord? Aren’t y’all proof of my work in Him?
Even if others doubt me, y’all know I’m legit—you’re my apostolic receipts in the Lord.
Here’s my defense to those checking my credentials:
Don’t we have the right to food and drink?
Don’t we have the right to bring a believing wife, like the other apostles and Jesus’ brothers and Peter?
Or is it just me and Barnabas who gotta work side hustles instead of living off ministry?
Who goes to war at their own expense? Who plants a vineyard and doesn’t eat the grapes? Who herds sheep and doesn’t drink the milk?
I’m not just talking human logic—doesn’t the law say the same?
Moses wrote, “Don’t muzzle the ox while it’s treading grain.” Was God talking about oxen—or us?
Yeah, it was written for us—because the one who plows and threshes should do it with hope of sharing the harvest.
If we planted spiritual seeds in you, is it wild to expect some material support?
Others have claimed this right over you—shouldn’t we even more? But we didn’t use it. We’d rather take the L than block the gospel.
Don’t you know those who work in the temple eat from the temple? Those who serve at the altar share in the offerings?
In the same way, the Lord said those who preach the gospel should live off the gospel.
But I haven’t used that right—and I’m not writing this to start now. I’d rather die than lose my brag that I preach for free.
Preaching the gospel isn’t a flex—it’s a must. If I don’t preach, I’m done.
If I do it willingly, I get a reward. If not, I’m still on assignment.
So what’s my reward? That I preach the gospel free of charge, without using my rights.
Though I’m free from everyone, I made myself a servant to all—to win more people.
To the Jews, I became like a Jew to win Jews. To those under the law, I acted like I was under it—even though I’m not.
To those outside the law, I became like one of them—though I’m still under Christ’s law—to win them too.
To the weak, I became weak to win the weak. I became all things to all people so I might save some.
I do all this for the gospel—so I can share in its blessings.
Don’t you know that in a race, all runners run—but only one gets the prize? Run like you’re trying to win.
Everyone who competes trains with discipline. They do it for a crown that fades—we do it for one that lasts forever.
So I don’t run aimlessly. I don’t shadowbox.
I discipline my body and make it my servant—so after preaching to others, I don’t get disqualified myself.
Fam, I don’t want you unaware—our ancestors were all under the cloud, passed through the sea,
got baptized into Moses in the cloud and sea,
ate the same spiritual food,
drank the same spiritual drink—from the rock that followed them. And that Rock was Christ.
But God wasn’t pleased with most of them—they got dropped in the desert.
These stories are warnings: don’t crave evil like they did.
Don’t be idolaters like them. Remember when they partied around the golden calf? “The people sat down to eat and drink, then turned up.”
Don’t sleep around like they did—23,000 dropped in one day.
Don’t test Christ, like some of them did—and got wrecked by snakes.
Don’t grumble like they did—and got taken out by the destroyer.
These things happened as examples—and were written down to warn us, the endgame generation.
So if you think you’re standing strong, watch out—you might fall.
No temptation’s hit you that’s not common. God’s faithful—He won’t let you be tempted beyond what you can handle. He’ll always give you a way out.
So fam, run from idolatry.
I’m talking to smart people—judge for yourselves what I’m saying.
The cup of blessing we bless—isn’t it sharing in Christ’s blood? The bread we break—isn’t it sharing in His body?
There’s one bread, and we’re one body—‘cause we all share that one loaf.
Look at Israel: those who eat the sacrifices are partners in the altar.
So what am I saying? That idols are real? That food offered to them means something?
Nah. What they offer, they offer to demons—not to God. I don’t want you linked with demons.
You can’t sip the Lord’s cup and the demon’s cup. Can’t eat at both tables.
You trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? You think you’re stronger than Him?
“I can do anything”—sure, but not everything’s helpful. Not everything builds people up.
Don’t just look out for yourself—look out for others too.
Eat whatever’s sold at the market—no need to interrogate it.
“The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it.”
If a non-believer invites you over and you wanna go, eat whatever’s served—no questions asked.
But if someone says, “This was offered to idols,” don’t eat it—for their sake and their conscience.
I’m talking about their conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by someone else’s conscience?
If I eat with thanks, why get dragged for something I’m grateful for?
So whether you eat, drink, or whatever—do it all for God’s glory.
Don’t trip up Jews, Greeks, or God’s church.
Just like me—I try to please everyone in every way. Not for me, but so many can be saved.
Copy me like I copy Christ.
I’m glad y’all remember me and hold tight to the traditions I passed on.
Here’s the order: Christ is the head of every man, man is the head of woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Every guy who prays or prophesies with his head covered disrespects his head.
Every girl who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disrespects hers—it’s like she shaved it off.
If she won’t cover her head, she might as well shave it. But since that’s shameful, she should cover it.
A man shouldn’t cover his head—he’s the image and glory of God. But woman is the glory of man.
Man didn’t come from woman—woman came from man.
Man wasn’t made for woman, but woman for man.
That’s why a woman should have a symbol of authority on her head—because of the angels.
Still, in the Lord, woman isn’t independent of man, and man isn’t independent of woman.
Woman came from man, but now man is born of woman—and all things come from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it cool for a woman to pray uncovered?
Doesn’t nature itself teach you that long hair on a guy is kinda disgraceful?
But if a girl has long hair, it’s her glory—it’s given as a natural covering.
If anyone wants to argue, just know this is how we roll—and all God’s churches do too.
Now, about your gatherings—I can’t praise you. They’re doing more harm than good.
First off, I hear there are divisions when y’all meet—and I kinda believe it.
There have to be factions, so the real ones can stand out.
When you come together, it’s not really the Lord’s Supper you’re eating.
Everyone’s diving into their own meal—some go hungry, others get lit.
Don’t y’all have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you despise God’s church and shame those with nothing? I can’t praise that.
I got this straight from the Lord and passed it on: the night Jesus was betrayed, He took bread,
gave thanks, broke it, and said, “This is my body, broken for you. Do this to remember me.”
Same with the cup after dinner: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Drink it to remember me.”
Every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you’re repping the Lord’s death—till He comes back.
So if you eat or drink unworthily, you’re guilty of disrespecting the body and blood of the Lord.
Check yourself before you eat the bread and drink the cup.
If you eat and drink without recognizing the body, you’re eating judgment on yourself.
That’s why many of you are weak, sick, and some have even died.
If we judged ourselves, we wouldn’t be judged.
But when the Lord judges us, it’s discipline—so we won’t be condemned with the world.
So fam, when you come together to eat, wait for each other.
If you’re hungry, eat at home—so your gathering doesn’t bring judgment. I’ll handle the rest when I get there.
Now about spiritual gifts, fam—I don’t want y’all clueless.
You remember when you were out there, chasing mute idols like lost sheep.
So I’m telling you: no one speaking by God’s Spirit says “Jesus is cursed,” and no one can say “Jesus is Lord” except by the Holy Spirit.
There’s different gifts, but the same Spirit.
Different ways to serve, but the same Lord.
Different kinds of work, but the same God powers them all.
The Spirit shows up in each of us for the squad’s good.
One gets wisdom, another knowledge—both from the same Spirit.
Another gets faith, another healing—still the same Spirit.
Another gets miracle power, another prophecy, another can tell spirits apart. One speaks in tongues, another interprets them.
One Spirit does all this—handing out gifts however He wants.
Just like the body’s one unit with many parts, so is Christ.
We were all baptized by one Spirit into one body—Jews, Greeks, slaves, free—and we all got the same Spirit drink.
The body isn’t just one part—it’s many.
If the foot says, “I’m not a hand, so I don’t belong,” that doesn’t make it any less part of the body.
If the ear says, “I’m not an eye, so I don’t belong,” it’s still part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, how would we hear? If all ears, how would we smell?
But God placed each part exactly where He wanted.
If all were one part, where’s the body?
But now there are many parts—one body.
The eye can’t say to the hand, “I don’t need you.” The head can’t say to the feet, “You’re irrelevant.”
In fact, the parts that seem weaker are actually essential.
The parts we think are less honorable—we treat with extra care.
God designed the body this way—giving more honor to the parts that lacked it,
so there’d be no division, and every part would care for the others.
If one part suffers, all suffer. If one part’s honored, all celebrate.
You are Christ’s body—and each of you is a part of it.
God set up the squad: apostles, prophets, teachers, miracle workers, healers, helpers, organizers, tongue-speakers.
Is everyone an apostle? Prophet? Teacher? Miracle worker?
Does everyone heal? Speak in tongues? Interpret?
Go after the greater gifts. But I’ll show you a way that’s even better…
I could speak every language—human and angelic—but if I don’t have love, I’m just loud static.
I could prophesy, know all mysteries, all knowledge, have faith to move mountains—but no love? I’m nothing.
I could give away everything, even die a martyr—but without love, it’s worthless.
Love is patient. Love is kind. It doesn’t envy. It doesn’t flex. It’s not arrogant.
It doesn’t act rude. It’s not selfish. It’s not easily triggered. It doesn’t keep receipts of wrongs.
Love doesn’t vibe with evil—but celebrates truth.
It always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always hangs on.
Love never fails. Prophecies? They’ll expire. Tongues? They’ll go quiet. Knowledge? It’ll fade.
We know in part and prophesy in part—
but when the full thing shows up, the partial gets retired.
When I was a kid, I talked, thought, and reasoned like one. But I grew up and put childish things away.
Now we see like a blurry mirror—but then, face to face. Now I know in part—then I’ll know fully, just like I’m fully known.
So now these three stay: faith, hope, and love. But the GOAT? Love.
Chase love like it’s the bag. And go hard for spiritual gifts—especially prophecy.
If you speak in tongues, you’re talking to God, not people—no one gets it. It’s Spirit-speak, mystery mode.
But if you prophesy, you’re speaking life—building people up, encouraging, and comforting.
Tongues build up the speaker. Prophecy builds up the squad.
I wish y’all spoke in tongues—but I’d rather you prophesy. Prophecy hits harder unless tongues get translated.
If I show up speaking in tongues, how’s that helping you—unless I drop a word of revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?
Even lifeless instruments—flute, harp—gotta play distinct notes or it’s just noise.
If the trumpet’s unclear, who’s gonna suit up for battle?
Same with y’all—if your tongue talk isn’t clear, who’s gonna get the message? You’re just talking into the air.
There’s all kinds of languages in the world—and they all mean something.
But if I don’t understand the language, I’m a foreigner to the speaker—and they to me.
So since you’re eager for spiritual gifts, aim to build up the church.
If you speak in tongues, pray for the gift to interpret too.
If I pray in tongues, my spirit’s lit—but my mind’s clueless.
So what do I do? I’ll pray with my spirit *and* my mind. I’ll sing with both too.
If you bless in the Spirit, how can someone who doesn’t understand say “Amen” if they don’t know what you said?
You might be giving thanks well—but it’s not helping them.
I thank God I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in church, I’d rather speak five clear words to teach others than 10,000 in tongues.
Fam, don’t be childish in your thinking. Be innocent in evil—but grow up in your minds.
Scripture says: “With foreign tongues and lips I’ll speak to this people, but they still won’t listen.”
So tongues are a sign for unbelievers—not believers. Prophecy is for believers—not unbelievers.
If the whole squad’s speaking in tongues and outsiders walk in, won’t they think you’ve lost it?
But if everyone’s prophesying and someone walks in, they’ll get exposed, convicted, and fall to their knees.
Their secrets get revealed, and they’ll say, “God is really here.”
So what’s the move, fam? When you gather, each one brings something—a song, a teaching, a tongue, a revelation, an interpretation. Let it all build the squad.
If anyone speaks in tongues, two or three max—one at a time—and someone must interpret.
If there’s no interpreter, zip it. Talk to God silently.
Let two or three prophets speak, and others weigh it.
If someone else gets a word while one’s speaking, the first should pause.
You can all prophesy one by one—so everyone learns and gets encouraged.
Prophetic spirit can control their own spirit.
‘Cause God isn’t about chaos—He’s about peace. That’s how it is in all the churches.
Women should stay chill in the gatherings—they’re not permitted to take over, but should stay in sync, like the law says.
If they wanna learn something, they should ask their husbands at home. It’s not the vibe for them to interrupt the gathering.
Did the word of God start with you? Or are you the only ones it reached?
If anyone thinks they’re a prophet or spiritual, they should recognize this command comes from the Lord.
If they ignore this, they’ll be ignored.
So fam, go after prophecy—and don’t shut down tongues.
But let everything be done properly and in order.
Let me remind y’all of the gospel I preached—the one you received, stand on, and are saved by.
If you hold tight to the message—unless you believed for nothing.
I passed on what I got first: Christ died for our sins, just like Scripture said.
He was buried. He rose on the third day—just like Scripture said.
He showed up to Peter, then the Twelve.
Then He appeared to over 500 people at once—most still alive, some have clocked out.
Then to James, then all the apostles.
Last of all, He showed up to me—like a late-born misfit.
I’m the least of the apostles—don’t even deserve the title, ‘cause I used to persecute God’s squad.
But by God’s grace, I am what I am. And that grace wasn’t wasted—I worked harder than all of them. But it wasn’t me—it was God’s grace in me.
So whether it’s me or them, this is what we preach—and what you believed.
Now if we preach Christ rose from the dead, how can some of y’all say there’s no resurrection?
If there’s no resurrection, then Christ didn’t rise.
And if Christ didn’t rise, our preaching is pointless—and so is your faith.
We’d be false witnesses about God—saying He raised Christ when He didn’t.
If the dead don’t rise, then Christ didn’t rise.
And if Christ didn’t rise, your faith is fake and you’re still stuck in sin.
Then those who died in Christ are just… gone.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we’re the most pitiful people on earth.
But Christ *did* rise—the firstfruits of those who’ve died.
Death came through one man—resurrection comes through another.
In Adam, all die. In Christ, all will be made alive.
But in order: Christ first, then those who belong to Him when He returns.
Then the end comes—when He hands the kingdom to God the Father, after shutting down every rule, authority, and power.
He must reign till He puts all enemies under His feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
God put everything under His feet. But obviously, God Himself isn’t under Christ.
When everything’s under Christ, He’ll hand it all back to God—so God will be all in all.
Otherwise, why do people get baptized for the dead? If the dead don’t rise, what’s the point?
And why are we risking our lives every day?
I swear, brothers and sisters, I die daily—by the pride I have in you through Christ Jesus.
If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for nothing, what’s the gain? If the dead don’t rise, “Let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
Don’t get it twisted: bad company corrupts good character.
Wake up! Live right! Stop sinning! Some of y’all don’t even know God—and I say that to your shame.
But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? What kind of body do they get?”
Foolish question. What you plant doesn’t grow unless it dies.
And what you plant isn’t the full plant—it’s just a seed.
But God gives it a body as He wants—each seed its own form.
Not all flesh is the same—humans, animals, birds, fish—they all differ.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly ones—each with its own glory.
The sun shines one way, the moon another, stars another—and even stars differ in brightness.
Same with resurrection: the body’s sown perishable, raised imperishable.
Sown in dishonor, raised in glory. Sown in weakness, raised in power.
Sown a natural body, raised a spiritual one. If there’s a natural body, there’s a spiritual one too.
Scripture says: “The first man, Adam, became a living being.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
The spiritual didn’t come first—the natural did. Then the spiritual.
The first man was from the dust. The second man is from heaven.
Earthlings are like the earthly man. Heaven-born are like the heavenly man.
Just like we wore the image of the earthly, we’ll wear the image of the heavenly.
Flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s kingdom. Perishable stuff can’t inherit the imperishable.
Listen up—I’m dropping a mystery: we won’t all die, but we’ll all be changed.
In a flash, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet—the dead will rise imperishable, and we’ll be changed.
This perishable body must put on the imperishable. This mortal must put on immortality.
When that happens, this Scripture hits: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”
“Where, O death, is your sting? Where’s your win, grave?”
The sting of death is sin. The power of sin is the law.
But thank God—He gives us the win through Jesus Christ our Lord.
So fam, stand firm. Be unshakable. Always overflow in the Lord’s work—‘cause you know it’s never wasted.
Now about the squad fund for the saints—do what I told the Galatian churches to do.
Every Sunday, each of you should set aside some cash, stacking it up as you prosper—so no last-minute scrambling when I come.
When I pull up, I’ll send whoever you trust with the gift to Jerusalem—with receipts and blessings.
If it makes sense for me to go too, we’ll roll together.
I’ll come through Macedonia—‘cause I’m passing through there anyway.
Maybe I’ll stay a while—or even winter with y’all—so you can help me on the next leg.
I don’t wanna just do a quick drive-by. If the Lord lets it happen, I’ll stay a bit.
But I’m staying in Ephesus till Pentecost—
‘Cause a big door’s wide open here, and yeah, there’s mad opposition.
If Timothy shows up, treat him right—he’s doing the Lord’s work just like me.
Don’t let anyone clown him. Send him off in peace so he can come to me—I’m expecting him with the crew.
About Apollos—I begged him to visit y’all with the brothers, but he didn’t feel led to come now. He’ll pull up when the time’s right.
Stay woke. Stand firm in the faith. Be brave. Be strong.
Let everything you do be soaked in love.
You know Stephanas and his people were the first to believe in Achaia—and they’ve dedicated themselves to serving the squad.
So show respect to folks like them—and to everyone grinding alongside them.
I’m hyped Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came—they filled the gap where y’all couldn’t.
They refreshed my spirit and yours. Show them love—they deserve it.
The churches in Asia send love. Aquila and Priscilla say what’s up, and so does the squad that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters here send love. Greet each other with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, wrote this part myself—signature vibes.
If anyone doesn’t love the Lord—let them be cut off. Maranatha. Come, Lord.
Grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Real talk. Amen.
